The '''2026 World Surf League''' is the 49th season of all iterations of the [[World Surf League|tour circuit for professional surfers]]. The first event of the tour was the [[Rip Curl Pro|Rip Curl Pro Bells Beach]], the longest running professional surfing competition in the world.<ref name=":1">{{cite web|title=2026 Rip Curl Pro Bells Beach|url=https://www.worldsurfleague.com/events/2026/ct/436/rip-curl-pro-bells-beach/main|access-date=19 November 2025|website=World Surf League|date=19 November 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

The competition format has changed. Starting in the 2026 season, the WSL Finals will no longer be held to decide the champion. The competition format will return to a points system, with the last event of the season returning to the iconic waves of [[Billabong Pipeline Masters|Pipeline]].<ref>{{cite web|title=World Surf League Announces Return to Pipeline for Championship Tour Finale Starting in 2026|url=https://www.worldsurfleague.com/posts/542489/world-surf-league-announces-return-to-pipeline-for-championship-tour-finale-starting-in-2026|access-date=19 November 2025|website=World Surf League|language=en}}</ref>

[[Yago Dora]] and [[Molly Picklum]] are the defending champions from the 2025 season.<ref name=":16">{{cite web|title=Molly Picklum, Yago Dora Win First World Titles in Historic Cloudbreak Surf|url=https://www.surfer.com/news/molly-picklum-yago-dora-win-2025-world-title-fiji-cloudbreak|website=SURFER Magazine|date=2 September 2025 |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":17">{{cite web|title=Molly Picklum wins first world surfing title with dominant display at WSL Finals|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2025/sep/02/wsl-world-surfing-finals-molly-picklum-australia-winnerk|website=The Guardian|date=2 September 2025 |language=en}}</ref> 36 men and 24 women are set to compete in the 2026 Championship Tour.<ref name=":3">{{cite web|title=World Surf League revamps Championship Tour format, putting Pipe Masters in the spotlight|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/olympics/news/world-surf-league-championship-tour-format-schedule|website=NBC Sports|date=2 May 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

In November 2025, the WSL announced that the 2026 Tour will see the return of four former world champions: [[Stephanie Gilmore]] and [[Carissa Moore]] in the women's tour, and [[Gabriel Medina]] and [[John John Florence]] in the men's tour. All four were awarded WSL CT Season Wildcards for 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=19 November 2025 |title=Stephanie Gilmore Set For Championship Tour Return in 2026 |url=https://www.worldsurfleague.com/posts/550214/stephanie-gilmore-set-for-championship-tour-return-in-2026 |website=World Surf League |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=19 November 2025 |title=Carissa Moore Announces Return to Championship Tour in 2026|url=https://www.worldsurfleague.com/posts/549882/carissa-moore-announces-return-to-championship-tour-in-2026|website=World Surf League |language=en}}</ref> In January 2026, John John Florence announced that he had ultimately decided to defer his CT return until 2027.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 January 2026 |title=John John Florence Defers Return to Competition, Announces Year-Long Break|url=https://www.worldsurfleague.com/posts/551788/john-john-florence-defers-return-to-competition-announces-year-long-break|website=World Surf League |language=en}}</ref> The wildcard spot previously given to John John Florence was subsequently awarded to [[Ramzi Boukhiam]], who missed the last three 2025 CT events prior to the Cut in 2025 due to a serious injury sustained during competition at Bells Beach.

The 2026 Championship Tour will span nine months and visit nine countries, with 13 events scheduled. The lineup includes a range of wave types-from barreling reef breaks like Pipeline, Cloudbreak, and Teahupo'o to performance-oriented locations such as Lower Trestles, Punta Roca, and Abu Dhabi. The schedule also features well-known stops like Snapper Rocks, Margaret River, Portugal, Saquarema, and opens at Bells Beach.<ref>{{cite web|title=2026 Championship Tour Event Schedule|url=https://www.worldsurfleague.com/events/2026/ct?all=1|access-date=19 November 2025|website=World Surf League|language=en}}</ref>

The 2026 CT will follow a new format that differs from those of previous years. Under the new system, 36 men and 24 women will compete in nine "regular-season" events, at which point the competition will be narrowed to 24 men  (top 22 competitors + 2 wildcards) and 16 women  (top 14 competitors + 2 wildcards) for the final three "postseason" events, during which competitors will be given the opportunity to accumulate more points. Surfers will carry only their best seven of nine results from the regular season into the next stage. For the first time in 5 years, there will be no mid-season cut.<ref name=":19">{{cite web|title=In 2026, the WSL Championship Tour is going back to the good old days|url=https://www.redbull.com/int-en/world-surf-league-wsl-schedule-calendar|website=RedBull|date=13 October 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

The nine "regular-season" events and three "postseason" events will be followed by a reimagined [[Billabong Pipeline Masters|Pipe Masters]] on the North Shore of [[O'ahu|O'ahu, Hawai'i]] as the thirteenth and final event of the tour, which will now award 15,000 points, 1.5 times more than a standard CT event.<ref name=":4">{{cite web|title=World Champions Will Once Again Be Crowned At Pipeline|url=https://www.surfer.com/news/pipeline-will-decide-world-champions|website=SURFER Magazine|date=2 May 2025 |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":11">{{cite web|title=Pipeline back as world surf tour finale in 2026|url=https://www.reuters.com/en/pipeline-back-world-surf-tour-finale-2026-2025-05-02/|website=Reuters|date=2 May 2025 |language=en}}</ref> The full 2026 men's and women's CT fields from the start of the season will rejoin the postseason competitors to compete in this final event.

In July 2026, the WSL announced that they had added an additional location to the CT schedule for 2026 to ensure a minimum of 12 events can be delivered during the season, should the [[Surf Abu Dhabi Pro]] be unable to run as scheduled as a result of the [[2026 Iran war]]. The event will be a third "postseason" event in addition to the two previously announced events in the UAE and Portugal.<ref name=":20">{{cite web|title=World Surf League Announces Cloud 9, Philippines As New Stop on 2026 Championship Tour Schedule|url=https://www.worldsurfleague.com/posts/557079/world-surf-league-announces-cloud-9-philippines-as-new-stop-on-2026-championship-tour-schedule/|website=World Surf League|date=1 July 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

In September, it was announced that the [[Surf Abu Dhabi Pro]] would no longer go ahead as a result of the war.<ref name=":21">{{cite web|title=WSL Cancels Surf Abu Dhabi Pro|url=https://www.theinertia.com/surf/wsl-cancels-surf-abu-dhabi-pro/|website=The Inertia|date=4 September 2026 |language=en}}</ref> “We explored every option to keep the Surf Abu Dhabi Pro on the calendar this year,” explained Ryan Crosby, WSL CEO. “Unfortunately, the current conditions and logistical limitations made it impossible for us to move forward. It was a difficult decision, but the right one at this time. We value our partnership with Surf Abu Dhabi, and look forward to returning.” As a result, the CT schedule returned to a 12 event season.

The final season rankings, and ultimately the World Titles, will be determined by a surfer's best nine of 12 results.

In another major change from previous years, elimination rounds have also been removed, meaning that if an athlete loses their first round heat at a given event, they will be eliminated from that event.<ref name=":15">{{cite web|title=World Surf League Announces Major Changes to World Tour Format in 2026|url=
https://www.hawaiiansouthshore.com/blogs/hawaiian-south-shore-surfing-blog/world-surf-league-announces-major-changes-to-world-tour-format-in-2026|website=Hawaiian South Shore|date=13 May 2025 |language=en}}</ref> According to WSL CEO Ryan Crosby, this change is intended to create "higher stakes from day one, with every heat carrying real consequence throughout the season."<ref name=":14">{{cite web|title=World Surf League Makes Major Changes, 2026 Schedule Revealed|url=
https://www.surfer.com/news/world-surf-league-2026-schedule|website=SURFER Magazine|date=28 July 2025 |language=en}}</ref> Under the new system, there will instead be a qualifying round, where the lower-seeded surfers will compete to face the higher-seeded athletes in the main event.<ref name=":27">{{cite web|title=A New Rule For The 2026 CT Season Puts Carissa, Steph, + John John At An Immediate Disadvantage|url=
https://stabmag.com/news/the-2026-ct-format-is-gloriously-cutthroat-2/|website=STAB Magazine|date=25 November 2025 |language=en}}</ref> For the men, seeds 29-36 will take part in the qualifying event, while the top 28 seeded athletes will move straight to the second round. For women, seeds 9-24 will take part in the qualifying rounds.

On 25 May 2026, the final day of the championship in New Zealand was halted after one of the photographers, Ed Sloane, was attacked by an unknown sea creature. Renato Hickel, the vice president of tours and competition said: "At this stage we are not certain if it was a [[shark]] or a [[sea lion]]."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sharma |first=Shweta |date=2026-05-25 |title=World Surf League halted after unknown sea creature attacks photographer |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/australasia/world-surf-league-photgrapher-bitten-sea-lion-shark-b2982960.html |access-date=2026-05-25 |website=[[The Independent]] |language=en}}</ref>

== Qualified athletes ==

The first nine events of the 2026 Championship Tour will be contested by the WSL top 36 men and top 24 women. In November 2024, the WSL announced an expansion of the number of female participants in the 2026 World Championship Tour (CT), increasing the roster from 18 to 24 surfers.<ref>{{cite web|title=WSL Announces Expanded Women's Field for 2026 Championship Tour|url=https://www.worldsurfleague.com/posts/536777/wsl-announces-expanded-women-s-field-for-2026-championship-tour|access-date=19 November 2025|website=World Surf League|language=en}}</ref>

The top 36 men consist of:

*The top 22 finishers from the 2025 Championship Tour rankings
*The top 10 finishers on the 2025 Challenger Series rankings
*Two WSL season wildcards
*Two event wildcards

The top 24 women consist of:

*The top 14 finishers on the 2025 Championship Tour rankings
*The top 7 finishers on the 2025 Challenger Series rankings
*Two WSL season wildcards
*One event wildcard

The first nine events will include 36 men and 24 women. After that, the field will be reduced to 24 men (top 22 competitors + 2 wildcards) and 16 women (top 14 competitors + 2 wildcards) for the final three postseason events in the Philippines, Abu Dhabi (prior to its cancellation) and Portugal. The top-ranked surfers will automatically requalify for the 2027 CT, as well as continue on to the second half of the Tour, where they will be joined by one men's and one women's season-long wildcard, and one men's and one women's event wildcard.*

== Schedule ==
The 2026 Championship Tour brings some changes to the calendar. All stages from the 2025 season will continue in 2026, with only the order of events changing, with the exception of the event in [[Jeffreys Bay|Jeffreys Bay, South Africa]], which has been replaced by the Corona Cero New Zealand in Raglan. The Australian leg that closed the mid-season cut is now the first three events of the CT.<ref name=":13">{{cite web|title=Australia to host first three events of 2026 WSL Champions Tour|url=
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2025-05-03/australia-to-host-first-three-events-of-2026-wsl-champions-tour/105247318|website=Australian Broadcasting Corporation|date=3 May 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

The first nine events define the "regular-season", while [[Surf Abu Dhabi Pro|Abu Dhabi]], [[Philippines Pro]] and [[MEO Rip Curl Pro Portugal|Portugal]] are considered the "postseason". Unlike in recent years, the WSL Finals is no longer the last event of the year. The [[Billabong Pipeline Masters|Pipeline Masters]] is once again the event where the 2026 world champions will be decided, with all competitors rejoining for the event.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=WSL 2026 Championship Tour Schedule & Format Changes - Pipeline Finale Returns|url=https://www.boardcovers.com.au/blog/wsl-2026-championship-tour-schedule-format-changes-pipeline-finale-returns/?srsltid=AfmBOor1coZ1u3WnyRSBY6o8aG8HMaT44KesbOVzDHWJulDrzVpUnsbd|access-date=21 November 2025|website=boardcovers|date=30 July 2025 |language=en}}</ref>
